html:
ABBA was a Swedish pop group formed in Stockholm in 1972 by Agnetha Fältskog, Björn Ulvaeus, Benny Andersson and Anni-Frid Lyngstad. They won the Eurovision Song Contest in 1974 with Waterloo.

Their songs, among them Dancing Queen, Mamma Mia and The Winner Takes It All, sold hundreds of millions of records. They were among the first acts from outside the English-speaking world to top charts in Britain and America. The group stopped recording in 1982.

The musical Mamma Mia! and its films brought their music to new generations, and they returned with a new album and a digital stage show in 2021. ABBA's success helped make Sweden one of the largest exporters of pop music, a line that runs to the songwriters behind many American hits and to Spotify. See Sweden.
